title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the neighbouring pages): (X,x) is a germ of differentiable surface. V = T_x(X) is its tangent plane, V* = V \ {0}, and S_x = V*/R*_+ is the circle of tangent directions. D*_x is the punctured germ, understood through the filter of punctured neighbourhoods of x. On the previous page Grothendieck builds a functor Θ (81) from germs of differentiable arcs at x to the fundamental groupoid Π_1(S_x). Each arc goes to its direction. Through Θ he gets an equivalence (94) between the category of coverings of the punctured germ D*_x and coverings of the circle S_x. He remarks that, given a local isomorphism f:(T_x X,0)->(X,x), everything reduces to a canonical construction inside a vector space V.

This page continues in that linear model.

(1) A half-line or direction Δ in V defines a germ of differentiable arc issuing from 0. That arc serves as a 'tangential base point' for the punctured germ D*_{V,0}. Hence it gives a corresponding pointed universal covering D*~_{V,0;Δ} of D*_{V,0}. Transporting by f gives a universal covering D*~_{x,Δ} of D*_x.

(2) He notes that one must check that D*~_{x,Δ} depends 'continuously' on Δ. Equivalently, the pointed universal cover V*~_Δ of V* must depend continuously on the base direction Δ. He calls this intuitively evident or standard: these covers form a covering of S_x, namely the family of path spaces.

(3) New step. Let u be a self-map (homeomorphism, after the struck-out 'difféomorphisme') of the germ (X,x) that fixes x and is differentiable at x. It induces:
- an automorphism u_{D*_x} of the punctured germ;
- an automorphism u_{S_x} of the circle of directions, namely the projectivised derivative du_x on V*/R*_+.

Choose a universal cover S~_x of S_x, and let D*~_x be the universal cover of D*_x associated to it by the equivalence (94). The page announces, and the next page states as (95), a canonical bijection. On one side are the germs of lifts of u_{D*} to D*~_x; on the other, the lifts of u_S to S~_x. The bijection is an isomorphism of T_x-torsors, where T_x ≅ Z is the orientation module of X at x, canonically identified with π_1 of S_x and of D*_x.

In modern terms: the local fundamental group at a puncture, together with tangential base points, is functorial for maps that are merely differentiable at the point. A lift of such a map to the universal cover of the punctured neighbourhood (its 'twist' or local rotation datum) is pinned down by the lift of its derivative's action on the circle of directions. This is the topological backbone of tangential base points and of the real oriented blow-up / Kato–Nakayama circle.

On the next page this leads to an axiomatic description, using arcs and convex cones in V and the 'voisinages abstraits'.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The 'continuity in Δ' is left as intuitively evident and not proved, and the bijection (95) is only announced on this page.

One hypothesis is delicate: u is only assumed differentiable at x. For u_{S_x} to be an automorphism, du_x must be invertible. Also, a lift on the punctured germ is only canonically matched to a lift on S_x via (94) once one knows that u maps arcs with direction Δ to arcs with direction du_x(Δ). That is true for any map differentiable at x with invertible derivative, but it needs to be stated.

missed.claim: Grothendieck works out, in purely differential-topological terms, the functoriality of tangential base points under maps that are only differentiable at the point. He makes the torsor of lifts on the punctured neighbourhood canonically isomorphic to the torsor of lifts of the derivative on the circle of directions. This prefigures the Kato–Nakayama / real oriented blow-up picture and links it to the local rotation theory of fixed points. The literature on tangential base points (Deligne, Ihara, Nakamura) is algebraic and does not usually state this differentiable-map version.
missed.quote: Soit maintenant u un [homéomorphisme] de X, fixant x, et différentiable en x. On a donc des automorphismes induits u_{D*_x} ... u_{S_x} ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a clean topological foundation for tangential base points and their behaviour under mapping classes and local homeomorphisms. That foundation is relevant to Grothendieck–Teichmüller actions and to dynamical rotation invariants at fixed points. It is, however, close to folklore.

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful foundational work on tangential base points and the circle of directions. The ideas are known (Deligne's tangential base points, the real oriented blow-up), and the differentiable-at-a-point functoriality is essentially folklore, though nicely formulated with orientation torsors.
transcription_corrections: 'Soit maintenant Y une' should read 'Soit maintenant u un'. The letter is u, as the later subscripts u_{D*_x}, u_{S_x} show.
The struck word is 'difféomorphisme'. The intended replacement, partly above the line, is probably 'homéomorphisme' (only differentiability at x is required).
'Δ dans V définit un germe d'arc (diff)' is correct. Δ is probably a half-line (demi-droite) of V.

The equation number before 'u_{D*_x} automorphisme de D*_x, u_{S_x} automorphisme de S_x' is unclear in the image (a '9?' with a possibly altered digit). '(93)' duplicates the previous page's (93), so it may be a different number.
The word on the line after 'intuitivement' looks like 'standard...' rather than 'évident'.
'S_x' should be written '$_x' (the slashed S symbol used for the circle of directions) in Grothendieck's notation, consistent with the previous page.
